translations.literal: The officiating invoker delivers the announcement — rites complete, music ended.
translations.idiomatic: The officiating invoker delivers the closing announcement — the rites are complete and the music has ended.

sentences.zh: 加牲兼幣，訖珣愈恭。

translations.literal: Adding sacrificial victims together with silks — upon completion, all the more reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Victims and silks are added together, and upon completion reverence grows ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 精神斯罄，惠澤無窮。

translations.literal: Spirit and essence are here fully offered — gracious blessings without end.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit and essence are fully given here, and gracious blessings know no end.

sentences.zh: 儲休錫美，萬福來崇。

translations.literal: Stored blessings bestowed in beauty — ten thousand felicities come to honor.
translations.idiomatic: Stored blessings are granted in splendor, and ten thousand blessings come to pay honor.

sentences.zh: 顏子考妣封謚

translations.literal: Posthumous Titles Granted to Yanzi's Father and Mother
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous Titles Granted to Yanzi's Father and Mother

sentences.zh: 宋五賢從祀

translations.literal: The Five Song Worthies Admitted to Associated Sacrifice
translations.idiomatic: The Five Song Worthies Admitted to Associated Sacrifice

sentences.zh: 至正十九年十一月，江浙行省據杭州路申備本路經歷司呈，準提控案牘兼照磨承發架閣胡瑜牒，嘗謂：

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the nineteenth year of Zhizheng, the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, acting on Hangzhou Circuit's report prepared by the circuit intendant's office and submitted forward, approving the dispatch of Hu Yu, associate control clerk and rubbing commissioner for outgoing dossiers and shelf archivist, who once stated:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the nineteenth year of Zhizheng, the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat received Hangzhou Circuit's report — prepared by the circuit intendant's office and forwarded upward — concerning a dispatch from Hu Yu, a control clerk and outgoing dossier commissioner, who had written:

sentences.zh: 文治興隆，宜舉行於曠典；

translations.literal: Literary governance flourishes — long-neglected canonical rites ought to be enacted;
translations.idiomatic: As literary governance flourishes, long-neglected canonical rites ought at last to be enacted;

sentences.zh: 儒先褒美，期激勵於將來。

translations.literal: Confucian forebears should be honored and praised — to inspire and encourage those yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian forebears should be honored and praised, so as to inspire and encourage generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 凡在聞知，詎容緘默。

translations.literal: All who have heard of this — how could one remain silent?
translations.idiomatic: All who have heard of this — how could one remain silent?

sentences.zh: 蓋國家化民成俗，莫先於學校；

translations.literal: For in transforming the people and establishing custom, nothing comes before schools;
translations.idiomatic: For in transforming the people and establishing custom, nothing comes before the schools;

sentences.zh: 而學校之設，必崇先聖先師之祀者，所以報功而示勸也。

translations.literal: And the establishment of schools necessarily exalts the sacrifices to the First Sage and First Teacher — this is how merit is repaid and encouragement shown.
translations.idiomatic: And in establishing schools, one must exalt the sacrifices to the First Sage and First Teacher — for this is how merit is repaid and encouragement shown.

sentences.zh: 我朝崇儒重道之意，度越前古。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's intent to honor Confucianism and esteem the Way surpasses earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's intent to honor Confucian learning and esteem the Way surpasses all earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 既已加封先聖大成之號，又追崇宋儒周敦頤等封爵，俾從祀廟庭，報功示勸之道，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: Having already added the title "Great Completion" to the First Sage, and posthumously ennobling Song Confucians such as Zhou Dunyi for associated sacrifice in the temple court — the way of repaying merit and showing encouragement can be called complete.
translations.idiomatic: Having already conferred the title "Great Completion" upon the First Sage, and posthumously ennobling Song Confucians such as Zhou Dunyi for associated sacrifice in the temple court, the way of repaying merit and showing encouragement can truly be called complete.

sentences.zh: 然有司討論未盡，尚遺先儒楊時等五人，未列從祀，遂使盛明之世，猶有闕典。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible offices' deliberations were incomplete — five forebears including Yang Shi still remain unlisted for associated sacrifice, so that even in this glorious age there is still a gap in the canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible offices' deliberations were incomplete: five forebears including Yang Shi still remain unlisted for associated sacrifice, so that even in this glorious age a gap in the canonical rites persists.

sentences.zh: 惟故宋龍圖閣直學士、謚文靖、龜山先生楊時，親得程門道統之傳，排王氏經義之謬，南渡後，朱、張、呂氏之學，其源委脈絡，皆出於時者也。

translations.literal: The former Song Dragon Hall Attendant Academician, posthumously honored as Wénjìng, Master Guishan Yang Shi — personally received the transmission of the Cheng school lineage, refuted the errors of the Wang clan's exegetical learning; after the southward crossing, the learning of Zhu, Zhang, and the Lü clan — their sources and branches all arose from Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song Dragon Hall attendant academician, posthumously honored as Wénjìng, Master Guishan Yang Shi personally received the transmission of the Cheng school lineage and refuted the errors of the Wang clan's exegetical learning; after the southward crossing, the learning of Zhu, Zhang, and the Lü clan — in source and branch alike — all arose from Shi.

sentences.zh: 故宋處士、延平先生李侗，傅河洛之學，以授朱熹，凡《集註》所引師說，即其講論之旨也。

translations.literal: The former Song recluse, Master Yanping Li Tong — transmitted the He-Luo learning to instruct Zhu Xi; all teacher's sayings cited in the "Collected Commentaries" are his discourses.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song recluse, Master Yanping Li Tong transmitted the He-Luo learning to Zhu Xi; every teacher's saying cited in the "Collected Commentaries" reflects his teaching.

sentences.zh: 故宋中書舍人、謚文定胡安國，聞道伊洛，志在《春秋》，纂為《集傳》，羽翼正經，明天理而扶世教，有功於聖人之門者也。

translations.literal: The former Song Secretariat Drafter, posthumously honored as Wéndìng Hu An'guo — learned the Way at Yi-Luo, devoted himself to the "Spring and Autumn Annals," compiled the "Collected Commentary," supporting the canonical classics, clarifying heavenly principle and upholding worldly teaching — one who served the Sage's gate with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song secretariat drafter, posthumously honored as Wéndìng Hu An'guo learned the Way at Yi-Luo and devoted himself to the "Spring and Autumn Annals," compiling the "Collected Commentary" to support the canonical classics, clarify heavenly principle, and uphold worldly teaching — a man who served the Sage's gate with great merit.

sentences.zh: 故宋處士、贈太師榮國公、謚文正、九峰先生蔡沈，從學朱子，親承指授，著《書集傳》，發明先儒之所未及，深有功於聖經者也。

translations.literal: The former Song recluse, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Duke of Rong State, posthumously honored as Wénzhèng, Master Jiufeng Cai Shen — studied under Master Zhu, personally received instruction, authored the "Collected Commentary on the Documents," elucidating what earlier Confucians had not reached — deeply meritorious to the holy scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song recluse, posthumously granted grand preceptor and duke of Rong State, posthumously honored as Wénzhèng, Master Jiufeng Cai Shen studied under Master Zhu and personally received his instruction, authoring the "Collected Commentary on the Documents" and elucidating what earlier Confucians had not reached — a man deeply meritorious to the holy scriptures.

sentences.zh: 故宋翰林學士、參知政事、謚文忠、西山先生真德秀，博學窮經，踐履篤實。

translations.literal: The former Song Hanlin Academician, Vice Grand Councillor, posthumously honored as Wénzhōng, Master Xishan Zhen Dexiu — broad learning exhausted the classics, practice solid and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song Hanlin academician and vice grand councillor, posthumously honored as Wénzhōng, Master Xishan Zhen Dexiu possessed broad learning that exhausted the classics and a practice that was solid and sincere.

sentences.zh: 當時立偽學之禁，以錮善類，德秀晚出，獨以斯文為己任，講習躬行，黨禁解而正學明。

translations.literal: At the time a ban on "False Learning" was instituted to cage good men; Dexiu emerged late, alone taking this cultural tradition as his charge — teaching and personal practice; when the factional ban was lifted, orthodox learning was clarified.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a ban on "False Learning" was instituted to suppress good men; Dexiu emerged late and alone took this cultural tradition as his personal charge — teaching and practicing it himself — and when the factional ban was lifted, orthodox learning was clarified.

sentences.zh: 此五人者，學問接道統之傳，著述發儒先之秘，其功甚大。

translations.literal: These five men — in learning they continued the transmission of the Way; in writing they disclosed the secrets of Confucian forebears — their merit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: These five men continued the transmission of the Way in their learning and disclosed the hidden teachings of Confucian forebears in their writings — their merit is very great.

sentences.zh: 況科舉取士，已將胡安國《春秋》、蔡沈《尚書集傳》表章而尊用之，真德秀《大學衍義》亦備經筵講讀，是皆有補於國家之治道者矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, in civil service examinations for selecting officials, Hu An'guo's "Spring and Autumn Annals" and Cai Shen's "Collected Commentary on the Documents" have already been proclaimed and honored in use; Zhen Dexiu's "Extension of the Meaning of the Great Learning" is also prepared for lecturing at the Classics Mat — all have contributed to the state's governance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in civil service examinations for selecting officials, Hu An'guo's "Spring and Autumn Annals" and Cai Shen's "Collected Commentary on the Documents" have already been proclaimed and honored in use, and Zhen Dexiu's "Extension of the Meaning of the Great Learning" is also prepared for lecturing at the Classics Mat — all of which have contributed to the state's governance.

sentences.zh: 各人出處，詳見《宋史》本傳，俱應追錫名爵，從祀先聖廟廷，可以敦厚儒風，激勸後學。

translations.literal: Each man's career is detailed in the biographies in the "History of Song"; all should be posthumously granted titles and ranks and admitted to associated sacrifice at the temple of the First Sage — this can deepen Confucian culture and encourage later students.
translations.idiomatic: Each man's career is detailed in the biographies in the "History of Song"; all should be posthumously granted titles and ranks and admitted to associated sacrifice at the temple of the First Sage — thereby deepening Confucian culture and encouraging later students.

sentences.zh: 如蒙備呈上司，申達朝省，命禮官討論典禮，如周敦頤等例，聞奏施行，以補闕典，吾道幸甚。

translations.literal: If we may fully memorialize our superiors, report to the provincial court, and order ritual officials to deliberate the canonical ceremony, following the precedent of Zhou Dunyi and others, and memorializing for implementation — to supplement the gap in canonical rites — our Way would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: If we may fully memorialize our superiors and report to the provincial court, ordering ritual officials to deliberate the canonical ceremony following the precedent of Zhou Dunyi and others and memorializing for implementation to supplement the gap in canonical rites, our Way would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 本省以其言具咨中書省，仍遣胡瑜赴都投呈。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat fully consulted the Central Secretariat on his words, and still dispatched Hu Yu to the capital to submit the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat fully consulted the Central Secretariat on his proposal and dispatched Hu Yu to the capital to submit the memorial.

sentences.zh: 至正二十一年七月，中書判送禮部，行移翰林、集賢、太常三院會議，俱準所言，回呈中書省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-first year of Zhizheng, the Central Secretariat forwarded it to the Ministry of Rites; circular letters were sent to the Hanlin Academy, Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices for joint conference — all approved his proposal, and replied to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-first year of Zhizheng, the Central Secretariat forwarded it to the Ministry of Rites and sent circular letters to the Hanlin Academy, Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices for joint conference; all approved his proposal and replied to the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十二年八月，奏準送禮部定擬五先生封爵謚號。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-second year, it was memorialized and approved; sent to the Ministry of Rites to determine the five masters' ennoblements and posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-second year, it was memorialized and approved and sent to the Ministry of Rites to determine the five masters' ennoblements and posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 俱贈太師。

translations.literal: All were posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: All were posthumously granted the title of grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 楊時追封吳國公，李侗追封越國公，胡安國追封楚國公，蔡沈追封建國公，真德秀追封福國公。

translations.literal: Yang Shi was posthumously ennobled Duke of Wu State, Li Tong Duke of Yue State, Hu An'guo Duke of Chu State, Cai Shen Duke of Jian State, Zhen Dexiu Duke of Fu State.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi was posthumously ennobled duke of Wu State, Li Tong duke of Yue State, Hu An'guo duke of Chu State, Cai Shen duke of Jian State, and Zhen Dexiu duke of Fu State.

sentences.zh: 各給詞頭宣命，遣官賫往福建行省，訪問各人子孫給付。

translations.literal: Each was given a formal patent and edict of appointment; officials were dispatched bearing them to the Fujian Branch Secretariat to visit each man's descendants and deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: Each was given a formal patent and edict of appointment, and officials were dispatched bearing them to the Fujian Branch Secretariat to visit each man's descendants and deliver them.

sentences.zh: 如無子孫者，於其故所居鄉里郡縣學，或書院祠堂內，安置施行。

translations.literal: Where there were no descendants, they were placed and implemented in the school of the former place of residence at the district or county level, or within an academy hall or ancestral shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Where there were no descendants, the patents were placed and implemented in the district or county school of the man's former place of residence, or within an academy hall or ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 朱熹加封齊國父追謚獻靖

translations.literal: Additional Ennoblement of Zhu Xi as Duke of Qi State; Posthumous Title Xiànjìng for His Father
translations.idiomatic: Additional Ennoblement of Zhu Xi as Duke of Qi State; Posthumous Title Xiànjìng for His Father

sentences.zh: 至正二十二年十二月，追謚朱熹父為獻靖，其制詞云：「考德而論時，灼見風儀之俊；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-second year of Zhizheng, the posthumous title Xiànjìng was conferred on Zhu Xi's father; the edict text reads: "Examining virtue and assessing the age, clearly seeing the excellence of his bearing;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-second year of Zhizheng, the posthumous title Xiànjìng was conferred on Zhu Xi's father; the edict text reads: "Examining his virtue and assessing his age, one clearly sees the excellence of his bearing;

sentences.zh: 觀子而知父，迨聞《詩》、《禮》之傳。

translations.literal: Knowing the father through the son — at last hearing the transmission of the "Odes" and "Rites."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the father through the son — at last one hears of the transmission of the "Odes" and "Rites."

sentences.zh: 久幽堂，丕昭公論。

translations.literal: Long hidden in the hall — now greatly clarified in public discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Long hidden in obscurity — now greatly clarified in public esteem.

sentences.zh: 故宋左承議郎、守尚書吏部員外郎、兼史館校勘、累贈通議大夫朱松，仕不躁進，德合中行。

translations.literal: The former Song Left Policy Adviser, Attendant Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Ministry of Works, concurrent Historiographer of the Historical Bureau, repeatedly granted General Purifier Zhu Song — in office not hasty in advancement, in virtue matching the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song left policy adviser, attendant director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Ministry of Works, concurrent historiographer of the Historical Bureau, and repeatedly granted general purifier Zhu Song — in office he was not hasty in advancement, and in virtue he matched the middle way.

sentences.zh: 溯鄒魯之淵源，式開來學；

translations.literal: Tracing the deep source of Zou and Lu — opening the way for coming learners;
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the deep source of Zou and Lu, he opened the way for generations of learners;

sentences.zh: 開圖書之蘊奧，妙契玄機。

translations.literal: Unfolding the hidden profundities of books and records — wonderfully accorded with subtle truth.
translations.idiomatic: Unfolding the hidden profundities of books and records, he wonderfully accorded with subtle truth.

sentences.zh: 奏對雖忤於權奸，嗣續篤生於賢哲。

translations.literal: Though memorials at court offended powerful villains, his succession faithfully produced worthy sages.
translations.idiomatic: Though his memorials at court offended powerful villains, his line faithfully produced worthy sages.

sentences.zh: 化民成俗，著書滿家。

translations.literal: Transforming the people and establishing custom — his writings filled the household.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming the people and establishing custom, his writings filled the household.

sentences.zh: 既繼誌述事之光前，何節惠易名之孔後。

translations.literal: Having already continued the previous generation's achievement in recording events — why was posthumous title and name-change so long delayed?
translations.idiomatic: Having already continued the previous generation's achievement in recording events, why was a posthumous title and change of name so long delayed?

sentences.zh: 才高弗展，嗟沈滯於下僚；

translations.literal: Though his talent was high and not fully displayed — alas, sunk in stagnation among lower officials;
translations.idiomatic: Though his talent was high and not fully displayed, alas, he sank in stagnation among lower officials;

sentences.zh: 道大莫容，竟昌明於永世。

translations.literal: Though the Way was great and not contained — ultimately it flourished clearly through eternal ages.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Way was great and found no full scope in his lifetime, ultimately it flourished clearly through eternal ages.

sentences.zh: 神靈不昧，休命其承。

translations.literal: His spirit is not obscured — this honored command let him receive it.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit is not obscured — let him receive this honored command.

sentences.zh: 可諡獻靖。」

translations.literal: May be posthumously titled Xiànjìng."
translations.idiomatic: May be posthumously titled Xiànjìng."

sentences.zh: 其改封熹為齊國公，制詞云：「聖賢之蘊載諸經，義理實明於先正；

translations.literal: The change of ennoblement for Xi to Duke of Qi State — the edict reads: "The store of sages and worthies is loaded in the classics; principle and righteousness are truly clarified by earlier worthies;
translations.idiomatic: In changing Xi Zhu's ennoblement to duke of Qi State, the edict reads: "The store of sages and worthies is loaded in the classics, and principle and righteousness are truly clarified by earlier worthies;

sentences.zh: 風節之厲垂諸世，褒崇豈間於異時。

translations.literal: Severe integrity handed down through generations — honor and praise should not differ with changing times.
translations.idiomatic: His stern integrity handed down through the ages — honor and praise ought not to vary with changing times.

sentences.zh: 不有巨儒，孰膺寵數？

translations.literal: Without such a great Confucian, who could receive such favor?
translations.idiomatic: Without such a great Confucian, who could receive such imperial favor?

sentences.zh: 故宋華文閣待制、累贈寶謨閣直學士、太師、追封徽國公、謚文朱熹，挺生異質，蚤擢科名。

translations.literal: The former Song Attendant Academician of the Huawen Hall, repeatedly granted Attendant Academician of the Baomo Hall, Grand Preceptor, posthumously ennobled Duke of Hui State, posthumously honored as Wén Zhu Xi — born with extraordinary qualities, early achieving examination rank.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song attendant academician of the Huawen Hall, repeatedly granted attendant academician of the Baomo Hall, grand preceptor, posthumously ennobled duke of Hui State, and posthumously honored as Wén Zhu Xi was born with extraordinary qualities and achieved examination rank at an early age.

sentences.zh: 試用於郡縣，而善政孔多；

translations.literal: Trial service in districts and counties — and good governance abounded;
translations.idiomatic: In trial service in districts and counties, good governance abounded;

sentences.zh: 回翔於館閣，而直言無隱。

translations.literal: Circulating among academy halls — and direct speech without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Circulating among academy halls, he spoke directly without concealment.

sentences.zh: 權奸屢挫，誌慮不回。

translations.literal: Powerful villains repeatedly thwarted him — his purpose and resolve unchanging.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful villains repeatedly thwarted him, yet his purpose and resolve never wavered.

sentences.zh: 著書立言，嘉乃簡編之富；

translations.literal: Composing books and establishing doctrine — blessed are his rich compilations;
translations.idiomatic: Composing books and establishing doctrine, blessed are his rich compilations;

sentences.zh: 愛君憂國，負其經濟之長。

translations.literal: Loving the ruler and worrying for the state — bearing his strength in statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Loving the ruler and worrying for the state, he bore his full strength in statecraft.

sentences.zh: 正學久達於中原，渙號申行於仁廟。

translations.literal: Orthodox learning long reached the Central Plains; proclamation of his title was declared under the Renzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Orthodox learning long reached the Central Plains, and proclamation of his title was declared under the Renzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 詢諸僉議，宜易故封。

translations.literal: Inquiring of all joint deliberation — the former ennoblement should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon inquiry of all joint deliberation, the former ennoblement should be changed.

sentences.zh: 國啟營丘，爰錫太公之境土；

translations.literal: The state opens Yingqiu — there bestowing the territory of Lord Tai;
translations.idiomatic: The state opens Yingqiu, there bestowing the territory of Lord Tai;

sentences.zh: 壤鄰洙泗，尚觀尼父之宮墻。

translations.literal: Its soil neighbors Zhu and Si — still viewing the walled precinct of the Father Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Its soil neighbors Zhu and Si, still within sight of the Father Ni's walled precinct.

sentences.zh: 緬想英風，載欽親命。

translations.literal: Remotely pondering his heroic spirit — greatly revering this personally conferred command.
translations.idiomatic: Remotely pondering his heroic spirit, we greatly revere this personally conferred command.

sentences.zh: 可追封齊國公，余並如故。」

translations.literal: May be posthumously ennobled Duke of Qi State; all else as before."
translations.idiomatic: May be posthumously ennobled duke of Qi State; all else as before."

sentences.zh: 國俗舊禮

translations.literal: National Customs and Former Rites
translations.idiomatic: National Customs and Former Rites

sentences.zh: 每歲，太廟四祭，用司禋監官一員，名蒙古巫祝。

translations.literal: Each year, at the four sacrifices of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one official of the Bureau of Sacrificial Observances was employed, styled the Mongol shaman-priest.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the Imperial Ancestral Temple's four seasonal sacrifices, one official from the Bureau of Sacrificial Observances served in the role called the Mongol shaman-priest.

sentences.zh: 當省牲時，法服，同三獻官升殿，詣室戶告腯，還至牲所，以國語呼累朝帝後名諱而告之。

translations.literal: When inspecting the sacrificial animals, in ritual vestments he ascended the hall together with the three offering officials, went to the chamber doors to announce fatness, returned to the place of the victims, and in the national language called out the taboo personal names of emperors and empresses of successive reigns and reported to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrificial animals were inspected, he put on ritual vestments, ascended the hall with the three offering officials, went to the chamber doors to announce that the victims were suitably fat, then returned to the slaughter site and, in Mongolian, called out the taboo names of emperors and empresses of successive reigns and reported to them.

sentences.zh: 明旦，三獻禮畢，獻官、御史、太常卿、博士復升殿，分詣各室，蒙古博兒赤跪割牲，太僕卿以朱漆盂奉馬乳酌奠，巫祝以國語告神訖，太祝奉祝幣詣燎位，獻官以下復版位載拜，禮畢。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, after the three offerings were complete, the offering officials, censor, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and academicians again ascended the hall, went separately to each chamber, a Mongol bööchü knelt and cut the victim, the Director of the Imperial Stud presented mare's milk in a red-lacquered basin as libation and offering, the shaman-priest in the national language reported to the spirits and finished, the Chief Invoker carried the prayer silks to the burning site, and the offering officials and those below returned to their ritual positions and performed full prostration bows; the rite was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day, once the three offerings were finished, the offering officials, the censor, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the academicians again ascended the hall and went separately to each chamber. A Mongol bööchü knelt to butcher the victim; the director of the imperial stud poured and offered mare's milk from a red-lacquered basin; the shaman-priest addressed the spirits in Mongolian and finished; the chief invoker carried the prayer silks to the burning pit; and the offering officials and all below returned to their marked positions and bowed in full prostration. The rite was then complete.

sentences.zh: 每歲，駕幸上都，以八月二十四日祭祀，謂之灑馬奶子。

translations.literal: Each year, when the imperial carriage visited Shangdu, sacrifices were performed on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month; this was called Sprinkling Mare's Milk.
translations.idiomatic: Each year when the emperor traveled to Shangdu, a sacrifice was held on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month, known as the Sprinkling Mare's Milk rite.

sentences.zh: 用馬一，羯羊八，彩段練絹各九匹，以白羊毛纏若穗者九，貂鼠皮三，命蒙古巫覡及蒙古、漢人秀才達官四員領其事，再拜告天，又呼太祖成吉思御名而祝之，曰：「托天皇帝福蔭，年年祭賽者。」

translations.literal: One horse, eight castrated rams, nine bolts each of colored silk brocade and bleached silk, nine bundles of white wool wrapped like ears of grain, and three sable pelts were used. A Mongol shaman-seer and four high officials—scholar-officials, both Mongol and Han—were ordered to preside over the affair. They bowed twice and reported to Heaven, then called out the imperial personal name of the founding ancestor Genghis and offered prayers, saying: "By the blessing and protection of the Heaven Emperor, [we perform] yearly sacrificial offerings."
translations.idiomatic: They used one horse, eight castrated rams, nine bolts each of colored silk brocade and bleached silk, nine sheaves of white wool wrapped like grain ears, and three sable pelts. A Mongol shaman-seer and four distinguished officials—Mongol and Han scholar-officials—were appointed to conduct the rite. They bowed twice to Heaven, then invoked the imperial personal name of the founding ancestor Genghis and prayed, saying, "By the blessing and protection of the Heavenly Emperor, may we offer sacrifice year after year."

sentences.zh: 禮畢，掌祭官四員，各以祭幣表裏一與之；

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the four officials in charge of the sacrifice were each given one set of sacrificial silks, outer and inner;
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, each of the four officials in charge of the sacrifice received one set of sacrificial silks, outer and inner layers included;

sentences.zh: 余幣及祭物，則凡與祭者共分之。

translations.literal: the remaining silks and sacrificial goods were then divided among all who had taken part in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: and the remaining silks and sacrificial goods were divided among everyone who had participated in the offering.

sentences.zh: 每歲，九月內及十二月十六日以後，於燒飯院中，用馬一，羊三，馬湩，酒醴，紅織金幣及裏絹各三匹，命蒙古達官一員，偕蒙古巫覡，掘地為坎以燎肉，仍以酒醴、馬湩雜燒之。

translations.literal: Each year, within the ninth month and after the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, in the food-burning courtyard, one horse, three sheep, mare's milk, sweet wine, three bolts each of red gold-woven silk and lining silk were used. One Mongol high official was ordered, together with a Mongol shaman-seer, to dig a pit in the ground and burn the meat, then also burn sweet wine and mare's milk together with it.
translations.idiomatic: Each year, sometime within the ninth month and again after the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, in the food-burning courtyard they used one horse, three sheep, mare's milk, sweet wine, and three bolts each of red gold-woven silk and lining silk. One Mongol high official, together with a Mongol shaman-seer, dug a pit in the ground to burn the meat, mixing sweet wine and mare's milk into the fire as well.

sentences.zh: 巫覡以國語呼累朝御名而祭焉。

translations.literal: The shaman-seer in the national language called out the imperial personal names of successive reigns and performed the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The shaman-seer invoked the imperial personal names of successive reigns in Mongolian and conducted the offering.

sentences.zh: 每歲，十二月下旬，擇日，於西鎮國寺內墻下，灑掃平地，太府監供彩幣，中尚監供細氈針線，武備寺供弓箭環刀，束稈草為人形一，為狗一，剪雜色彩段為之腸胃，選達官世家之貴重者交射之。

translations.literal: Each year, in the latter part of the twelfth month, on a chosen day, beneath the inner wall of the Western Zhenguo Temple, the ground was swept clean. The Directorate of the Imperial Household supplied colored silks; the Directorate of Palace Attendants supplied fine felt and needle and thread; the Directorate of Military Equipment supplied bows, arrows, and ring-handled sabers. One human figure and one dog were bound from straw, and their entrails were cut from scraps of colored silk brocade. Distinguished high officials from noble lineages were selected to shoot at them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the latter part of the twelfth month, on a chosen day, they swept clean a level space beneath the inner wall of the Western Zhenguo Temple. The Directorate of the Imperial Household supplied colored silks, the Directorate of Palace Attendants supplied fine felt and sewing materials, and the Directorate of Military Equipment supplied bows, arrows, and ring-handled sabers. They bound one human figure and one dog from straw and fashioned their entrails from scraps of colored silk. Noble high officials from distinguished families were chosen to take turns shooting at them.

sentences.zh: 非別速、劄剌爾、乃蠻、忙古、臺列班、塔達、珊竹、雪泥等氏族，不得與列。

translations.literal: Unless one belonged to the clans Besud, Jarchud, Naiman, Mangghud, Taileban, Tatar, Shanzhu, Sheni, and the like, one was not permitted to join the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Only members of the Besud, Jarchud, Naiman, Mangghud, Taileban, Tatar, Shanzhu, Sheni, and related clans were allowed to take part.

sentences.zh: 射至糜爛，以羊酒祭之。

translations.literal: When they had been shot to pulpy ruin, sheep and wine were used to sacrifice to them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the figures had been shot to pieces, they were offered sheep and wine in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，帝後及太子嬪妃並射者，各解所服衣，俾蒙古巫覡祝贊之。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was complete, the empress, consorts, crown prince's consorts, and the archers each removed the garments they were wearing and had Mongol shaman-seers offer blessings over them.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice, the empress, consorts, the crown prince's consorts, and the archers each removed the clothes they were wearing and had Mongol shaman-seers bless them.

sentences.zh: 祝贊畢，遂以與之，名曰脫災。

translations.literal: When the blessings were finished, the garments were then given to them; this was called Shedding Calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the blessing was finished, the garments were given to them; the rite was called Shedding Calamity.

sentences.zh: 國俗謂之射草狗。

translations.literal: In the national custom it was called Shooting the Straw Dog.
translations.idiomatic: In Mongol custom this was called Shooting the Straw Dog.

sentences.zh: 每歲，十二月十六日以後，選日，用白黑羊毛為線，帝後及太子，自頂至手足，皆用羊毛線纏系之，坐於寢殿。

translations.literal: Each year, after the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, on a chosen day, white and black sheep's wool was made into thread. The empress and crown prince, from crown to hands and feet, were all bound with wool thread and seated in the sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: Each year after the sixteenth day of the twelfth month, on a chosen day, they made thread from white and black sheep's wool and bound the empress and crown prince from head to hands and feet with it, seating them in the sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 蒙古巫覡念咒語，奉銀槽貯火，置米糠於其中，沃以酥油，以其煙薰帝之身，斷所系毛線，納諸槽內。

translations.literal: The Mongol shaman-seer recited incantations, presented a silver trough holding fire, placed rice bran in it, poured clarified butter over it, and with its smoke fumigated the emperor's body; the bound wool threads were cut and put into the trough.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol shaman-seer recited incantations, brought forward a silver trough containing fire, put rice bran in it, poured clarified butter over the bran, and fumigated the emperor's body with the smoke. The wool threads that had been bound on him were cut and cast into the trough.

sentences.zh: 又以紅帛長數寸，帝手裂碎之，唾之者三，並投火中。

translations.literal: A piece of red silk several inches long was also taken; the emperor tore it to pieces by hand, spat upon it three times, and all was cast into the fire.
translations.idiomatic: They also took a strip of red silk several inches long; the emperor tore it apart by hand, spat on it three times, and threw it all into the fire.

sentences.zh: 即解所服衣帽付巫覡，謂之脫舊災、迎新福云。

translations.literal: He then removed the cap and garments he was wearing and gave them to the shaman-seer; this was called shedding old calamity and welcoming new fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He then removed the cap and clothes he was wearing and gave them to the shaman-seer; the rite was called shedding old calamity and welcoming new fortune.

sentences.zh: 凡后妃妊身，將及月辰，則移居於外氈帳房。

translations.literal: Whenever an empress or consort was pregnant and the month of delivery drew near, she moved to an outer felt tent dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an empress or consort was pregnant and her due month approached, she moved into an outer felt tent.

sentences.zh: 若生皇子孫，則錫百官以金銀彩段，謂之撒答海。

translations.literal: If a prince or imperial grandson was born, the hundred officials were bestowed gold, silver, and colored silk brocade; this was called sadaq.
translations.idiomatic: If a prince or imperial grandson was born, officials were rewarded with gold, silver, and colored silk brocade in what was called the sadaq gift.

sentences.zh: 及彌月，復還內寢。

translations.literal: When the full month was reached, she returned again to the inner sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the full month had passed, she returned to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 其帳房則以頒賜近臣云。

translations.literal: The tent dwelling was then distributed as a gift to close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The tent was then bestowed on a close minister.

sentences.zh: 凡帝後有疾危殆，度不可愈，亦移居外氈帳房。

translations.literal: Whenever an emperor or empress fell gravely ill and recovery was judged impossible, he or she likewise moved to an outer felt tent dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an emperor or empress fell gravely ill and recovery seemed impossible, he or she likewise moved to an outer felt tent.

sentences.zh: 有不諱，則就殯殮其中。

translations.literal: If death occurred, encoffining and dressing were performed there.
translations.idiomatic: If death came, the body was encoffined and prepared for burial there.

sentences.zh: 葬後，每日用羊二次燒飯以為祭，至四十九日而後已。

translations.literal: After burial, twice each day sheep were used for food-burning offerings as sacrifice, continuing until the forty-ninth day and then ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: After burial, food-burning offerings with sheep were made twice daily until the forty-ninth day, when they ceased.

sentences.zh: 其帳房亦以賜近臣云。

translations.literal: The tent dwelling was likewise bestowed on a close minister.
translations.idiomatic: The tent was likewise given to a close minister.

sentences.zh: 凡宮車晏駕，棺用香楠木，中分為二，刳肖人形，其廣狹長短，僅足容身而已。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage came to rest, the coffin was of fragrant nanmu wood, split in two down the middle and hollowed in the likeness of the human form; its width, narrowness, length, and shortness were just enough to contain the body.
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor died, the coffin was made of fragrant nanmu wood, split in two and hollowed to the shape of the body, just large enough to hold the corpse and no more.

sentences.zh: 殮用貂皮襖、皮帽，其靴襪、系腰、盒缽，俱用白粉皮為之。

translations.literal: For dressing the corpse there were a sable-fur coat and fur cap; boots, socks, belt, box, and bowl were all made of white tanned leather.
translations.idiomatic: The body was dressed in a sable-fur coat and fur cap; boots, socks, belt, box, and bowl were all made of white tanned leather.

sentences.zh: 殉以金壺瓶二，盞一，碗碟匙箸各一。

translations.literal: For burial accompaniments there were two gold ewer-flasks, one cup, and one each of bowl, dish, spoon, and chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Burial goods included two gold ewer-flasks, one cup, and one bowl, dish, spoon, and pair of chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 殮訖，用黃金為箍四條以束之。

translations.literal: When dressing was complete, four bands of gold were used to bind it.
translations.idiomatic: When the body had been prepared, four gold bands were used to bind the coffin.

sentences.zh: 輿車用白氈青緣納失失為簾，覆棺亦以納失失為之。

translations.literal: The funeral carriage used white felt with blue-edged nashiji as curtains; the coffin covering was also made of nashiji.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral carriage had curtains of white felt edged in blue nashiji cloth, and the coffin covering was also made of nashiji.

sentences.zh: 前行，用蒙古巫媼一人，衣新衣，騎馬，牽馬一匹，以黃金飾鞍轡，籠以納失失，謂之金靈馬。

translations.literal: Going before, one Mongol shamaness was employed, dressed in new clothes, riding a horse and leading another horse whose saddle and bridle were adorned with gold and covered with nashiji; this was called the Golden Spirit Horse.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of the procession walked one Mongol shamaness in new clothes, mounted on a horse and leading another whose saddle and bridle were adorned with gold and draped in nashiji; this horse was called the Golden Spirit Horse.

sentences.zh: 日三次，用羊奠祭。

translations.literal: Three times each day sheep were used in libation and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep were offered in sacrifice three times each day.

sentences.zh: 至所葬陵地，其開穴所起之土成塊，依次排列之。

translations.literal: When they reached the burial mound site, the earth dug from opening the grave and piled up in clods was arranged in order.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial burial ground, the clods of earth dug from the grave opening were set out in order.

sentences.zh: 棺既下，復依次掩覆之。

translations.literal: Once the coffin had been lowered, the clods were again covered over in order.
translations.idiomatic: After the coffin was lowered, the clods were replaced in order to cover the grave.

sentences.zh: 其有剩土，則遠置他所，送葬官三員，居五里外。

translations.literal: If any earth remained, it was placed far away elsewhere. Three officials attending the funeral stayed five li outside.
translations.idiomatic: Any remaining earth was carried far off and deposited elsewhere. Three officials who had attended the funeral remained five li away.

sentences.zh: 日一次燒飯致祭，三年然後返。

translations.literal: Once each day food-burning offerings were made in sacrifice; after three years they then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They made food-burning offerings once each day, and only after three years did they return.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元七年，以帝師八思巴之言，於大明殿御座上置白傘蓋一，頂用素段，泥金書梵字於其上，謂鎮伏邪魔獲安國剎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Zhiyuan reign of Emperor Shizu, on the word of the Imperial Preceptor Phags-pa, one white parasol canopy was placed on the imperial throne in the Hall of Great Brilliance; its top was of plain silk, with Sanskrit characters written on it in gold paste, called Subduing Evil Demons and Securing Peace for the State and Buddhist Temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Zhiyuan reign, on the advice of the Imperial Preceptor Phags-pa, a white parasol canopy was placed on the imperial throne in the Hall of Great Brilliance. Its crown was of plain silk, with Sanskrit characters written on it in gold paste, intended to subdue evil demons and secure peace for the state and the Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 自後每歲二月十五日，於大明殿啟建白傘蓋佛事，用諸色儀仗社直，迎引傘蓋，周遊皇城內外，雲與眾生祓除不祥，導迎福祉。

translations.literal: Thereafter, each year on the fifteenth day of the second month, a White Parasol Buddhist service was inaugurated in the Hall of Great Brilliance. Various-colored ceremonial regalia and ritual procession units were used to welcome and escort the parasol canopy in a circuit tour inside and outside the imperial city, said to cleanse all living beings of ill fortune and usher in blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, each year on the fifteenth day of the second month, a White Parasol Buddhist service was held in the Hall of Great Brilliance. Regalia and ritual procession units of every color welcomed and escorted the parasol canopy on a circuit through the imperial city, said to cleanse all living beings of ill fortune and bring blessings.

sentences.zh: 歲正月十五日，宣政院同中書省奏，請先期中書奉旨移文樞密院，八衛撥傘鼓手一百二十人，殿後軍甲馬五百人，擡舁監壇漢關羽神轎軍及雜用五百人。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the first month each year, the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs jointly memorialized with the Secretariat, requesting that beforehand the Secretariat, by imperial command, send a formal notice to the Privy Council to allocate from the Eight Guards one hundred twenty umbrella-and-drum performers, five hundred armored cavalry of the rear guard, and five hundred bearers for the Han deity Guan Yu spirit palanquin of altar supervision and for miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the fifteenth day of the first month, the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs and the Secretariat jointly memorialized, asking that the Secretariat first issue an imperial order to the Privy Council to detail from the Eight Guards one hundred twenty umbrella-and-drum performers, five hundred armored rear-guard cavalry, and five hundred bearers for the spirit palanquin of the Han deity Guan Yu at the altar and for other miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 宣政院所轄官寺三百六十所，掌供應佛像、壇面、幢幡、寶蓋、車鼓、頭旗三百六十壇，每壇擎執擡舁二十六人，鈸鼓僧一十二人。

translations.literal: The three hundred sixty official temples under the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs supplied Buddha images, altar platforms, banners, streamers, jeweled canopies, carriage drums, and leading flags for three hundred sixty altars; each altar had twenty-six persons to bear, hold, and lift, and twelve cymbal-and-drum monks.
translations.idiomatic: The three hundred sixty official temples under the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs supplied Buddha images, altar platforms, banners, streamers, jeweled canopies, carriage drums, and leading flags for three hundred sixty altars. Each altar required twenty-six bearers and twelve cymbal-and-drum monks.

sentences.zh: 大都路掌供各色金門大社一百二十隊，教坊司雲和署掌大樂鼓、板杖鼓、篳篥、龍笛、琵琶、箏、緌七色，凡四百人。

translations.literal: The Dadu Circuit supplied one hundred twenty companies of various-colored Golden Gate grand ritual societies. The Yunhe Section of the Court Entertainment Office supplied seven kinds of instruments—great music drums, clapper-staff drums, bili pipes, dragon flutes, pipa lutes, zithers, and sui cords—for a total of four hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadu Circuit supplied one hundred twenty companies of Golden Gate grand ritual societies in various colors. The Yunhe Section of the Court Entertainment Office provided seven kinds of instruments—great drums, clapper-staff drums, bili pipes, dragon flutes, pipa, zithers, and sui cords—for a total of four hundred musicians.

sentences.zh: 興和署掌妓女雜扮隊戲一百五十人，祥和署掌雜把戲男女一百五十人，儀鳳司掌漢人、回回、河西三色細樂，每色各三隊，凡三百二十四人。

translations.literal: The Xinghe Section supplied one hundred fifty actresses in mixed costume troupe performances; the Xianghe Section supplied one hundred fifty men and women in miscellaneous variety acts; the Court Music Office supplied refined music in three colors—Han, Hui, and Hexi—three companies of each, for a total of three hundred twenty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinghe Section provided one hundred fifty actresses in mixed-costume troupe performances; the Xianghe Section provided one hundred fifty men and women in variety acts; and the Court Music Office provided refined music in Han, Hui, and Hexi styles, three companies of each, for a total of three hundred twenty-four musicians.

sentences.zh: 凡執役者，皆官給鎧甲袍服器仗，俱以鮮麗整齊為尚，珠玉金繡，裝束奇巧，首尾排列三十餘里。

translations.literal: All who performed service were given armor, robes, and ceremonial weapons by the state; bright splendor and neat order were prized above all, with pearls, jade, gold embroidery, and marvelously wrought adornments, the procession from head to tail extending more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: All participants were supplied by the state with armor, robes, and ceremonial weapons. Bright colors and perfect order were prized above all, with pearls, jade, gold embroidery, and fantastically wrought adornments; the procession stretched more than thirty li from front to rear.

sentences.zh: 都城士女，閭閻聚觀。

translations.literal: Men and women of the capital city gathered in the lanes and wards to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women of the capital crowded the streets and wards to watch.

sentences.zh: 禮部官點視諸色隊仗，刑部官巡綽喧鬧，樞密院官分守城門，而中書省官一員總督視之。

translations.literal: Officials of the Ministry of Rites inspected the various-colored companies and regalia; officials of the Ministry of Justice patrolled to restrain disorder; officials of the Privy Council were assigned to guard the gates in sections; and one official of the Secretariat supervised the whole.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Ministry of Rites inspected the various-colored companies and regalia; officials of the Ministry of Justice patrolled to keep order; officials of the Privy Council were posted at the gates; and one Secretariat official supervised the entire affair.

sentences.zh: 先二日，於西鎮國寺迎太子遊四門，舁高塑像，具儀仗入城。

translations.literal: Two days beforehand, at the Western Zhenguo Temple the crown prince was welcomed in a tour of the four gates; a tall statue was carried, and with full ceremonial regalia they entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before, at the Western Zhenguo Temple they welcomed the crown prince in a tour of the four gates, carrying a tall statue and entering the city with full ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 十四日，帝師率梵僧五百人，於大明殿內建佛事。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day, the Imperial Preceptor led five hundred Sanskrit monks in establishing a Buddhist service inside the Hall of Great Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day, the Imperial Preceptor led five hundred Sanskrit monks in conducting a Buddhist service inside the Hall of Great Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 至十五日，恭請傘蓋於御座，奉置寶輿，諸儀衛隊仗列於殿前，諸色社直暨諸壇面列於崇天門外，迎引出宮。

translations.literal: On reaching the fifteenth day, the parasol canopy was reverently requested from the imperial throne and placed on the jeweled palanquin; all ceremonial guards and regalia were arrayed before the hall, and the various-colored ritual procession units together with the altar platforms were drawn up outside the Gate of Veneration of Heaven, welcoming and escorting it out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day, the parasol canopy was reverently taken from the imperial throne and placed on the jeweled palanquin. All ceremonial guards and regalia were drawn up before the hall, and the various-colored ritual procession units and altar platforms were arrayed outside the Gate of Veneration of Heaven to welcome and escort it out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 至慶壽寺，具素食，食罷起行，從西宮門外垣海子南岸，入厚載紅門，由東華門過延春門而西。

translations.literal: They reached Qing Shou Temple, where a vegetarian meal was prepared; when the meal was finished they set out, proceeding from the southern bank of the lake outside the western palace gate wall, entering the Houzai Red Gate, passing through the East Flowery Gate and the Gate of Extended Spring, and turning west.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Qing Shou Temple, where a vegetarian meal was served. When the meal was finished they set out along the southern bank of the lake outside the western palace wall, entered the Houzai Red Gate, passed through the East Flowery Gate and the Gate of Extended Spring, and turned west.

sentences.zh: 帝及后妃公主，於玉德殿門外，搭金脊吾殿彩樓而觀覽焉。

translations.literal: The emperor, empress, consorts, and princesses, outside the Gate of the Hall of Jade Virtue, erected a colored viewing pavilion with a golden ridge at Wudian from which to observe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, empress, consorts, and princesses watched from a colored viewing pavilion with a golden ridge erected outside the Gate of the Hall of Jade Virtue.

sentences.zh: 及諸隊仗社直送金傘還宮，復恭置禦榻上。

translations.literal: When the various companies, regalia, and ritual procession units had escorted the golden parasol back to the palace, it was again reverently placed upon the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: When the various companies, regalia, and ritual procession units had escorted the golden parasol back to the palace, it was reverently replaced on the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 帝師僧眾作佛事，至十六日罷散。

translations.literal: The Imperial Preceptor and the monastic assembly performed the Buddhist service, which was dismissed and dispersed on the sixteenth day.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Preceptor and the monastic assembly conducted the Buddhist service, which concluded on the sixteenth day.

sentences.zh: 歲以為常，謂之游皇城。

translations.literal: This was performed yearly as a regular observance; it was called Touring the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: This became an annual observance, known as Touring the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 或有因事而輟，尋復舉行。

translations.literal: Sometimes it was suspended because of some affair, but soon afterward it was performed again.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes it was suspended for some reason, but was soon resumed.

sentences.zh: 夏六月中，上京亦如之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, the same was done at Shangdu as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, the same ceremony was held at Shangdu.
